tool_input.description: Run scratch program against WordUtils.wrap to verify exact output

result:
Only the one bug-revealing test remains failing. All 57 tests compile and run; 56 pass.

## Summary

I added `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/text/WordUtilsAgentTest.java` with 57 self-contained JUnit 5 test methods covering every public method of `WordUtils` (`capitalize`, `capitalizeFully`, `containsAllWords`, `initials`, `swapCase`, `uncapitalize`, all three `wrap` overloads, and the constructor), including null/empty/boundary cases and delimiter edge cases.

**1 failing test shows a real bug:**

- `testWrapFull_wrapLongWordsTrue` — `WordUtils.wrap("...https://commons.apache.org", 20, "\n", true, " ")` should produce `"...https://commons.apach\ne.org"` per the javadoc example, which is repeated identically across all three `wrap(...)` overloads' documentation. Instead, the implementation produces `"...https://commons.apac\nhe.org"` — the forced long-word-wrap branch (`wrappedLine.append(str, offset, wrapLength + offset)`) cuts the chunk one character short of the length consistently documented and illustrated in the class's own javadoc.

The other three initially-failing tests were my own mistakes (misreading ambiguous/self-contradicting javadoc lines like `uncapitalize(*, null) = *` and assuming `wrapLongWords` splits mid-word even when `false`); I corrected those three to match the class's actual, documented, and internally consistent behavior, and they now pass.
